expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.

expectations_used.reflect: Explains why releasing the original count created phantom stock and how the remaining-count fix prevents it.

summary: The candidate jumped almost immediately to the sweep file on a hunch, made a single edit, and reran tests until green, all within about two minutes. There was no explicit hypothesis about the release-quantity mechanism, no narration during the edit, and no post-fix explanation of why the bug occurred.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate moved straight to a location guess about the sweep file without reading the failing test body or asking about partially-shipped hold semantics, which is exactly the ambiguity this bug hinges on. No clarifying question was raised before editing began.

The stated plan was only a location guess ('something in the sweep file'), not a mechanism; per the rubric, naming a location and calling it 'poking around' does not meet the bar of identifying that the sweep releases original rather than remaining units. No hypothesis specific enough to be falsifiable was voiced before editing.

Aside from the opening guess and a closing remark, there is no narration of what was read, suspected, or tried during the actual edit-and-save stretch. An interviewer following only the transcript would not know what change was made or why.

A single, scoped edit was made to the implicated file and saved, and it resulted in the suite passing, suggesting the change was on-target. There is no evidence of thrashing or contradictory edits, but also no visible reasoning connecting the edit to a stated mechanism, so quality of the implementation choice can't be fully judged beyond its outcome.

The candidate reran the full test suite after the edit and confirmed a pass before ending the session, satisfying the minimum verification bar since the run covered the previously-failing test and others. There was no additional edge-case reasoning or explicit check that full-release behavior was unaffected beyond the aggregate green result.

The closing remark was a bare acknowledgment that tests passed, with no articulation of the root cause (original vs. remaining unit count) or why the edit fixed it. This treats the green run as the goal itself rather than explaining the underlying mechanism.
